title: Arkadelphia’s water
lead: Arkadelphia owns its water and sewer system. It is run by the city and paid for by water and sewer bills, not taxes. Nearby systems buy water from it too.

facts.v: The Ouachita River. The state rates it “low susceptibility to contamination.”
The City of Arkadelphia (state public water system AR0000085), governed by the city board.
Caddo Valley and two nearby systems (listed as Country Water and River Valley) buy wholesale water — 18.8% of water sales.
Three oxidation ponds, then a final pond where plastic frames contain duckweed. It discharges to the Ouachita River (state permit AR0020605, through Oct 2028).
$6,880,375 of revenue bonds, paid through 2052. In 2023 the utility took in $3,433,297 and spent $3,532,653 running it — a $99,356 operating loss — with a clean audit.
The 991-acre Southwest Arkansas Mega Site broke ground in July 2025 near Gum Springs, where Arkadelphia took over the water system in 2020 (with a $2,766,900 state loan, $766,900 of it forgiven).
Arkadelphia’s water-loss rate is not published (Docket #12).

quality.lead: The latest report posted by the state is for 2023. It shows no health-limit violations.

rows.note: The report lists a range with the top at 85 ppb. The 80 ppb limit applies to the running annual average at each monitoring site (40 CFR 141 Subpart V), so a single reading above 80 is not a violation by itself. The report shows no violation. These form when chlorine meets organic matter from the river.
2 of 30 homes tested were over the action level.

quality.violation: One paperwork violation: bacteria test results weren’t submitted for March 2023. The city resumed sending them.
quality.inspection: The state’s January 2024 sewer-plant inspection rated it “Satisfactory,” with two violations: the aerators in the first lagoon weren’t running, and a flowmeter was past its calibration date.
quality.note: The city’s own link to a 2024 report returned “not found” on Sept 26, 2026.

question: The documents do not yet say who would pay to expand water and sewer if a large industrial user locates at the Mega Site (Docket #16).
